actions.justification: Mandatory first step: continuous monitoring of HR, BP, SpO2, and RR per AHA guidelines for acute chest pain assessment.
Mandatory: AHA Class I recommendation to obtain 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of presentation to identify ST changes and differentiate STEMI from NSTEMI.
Mandatory: Immediate history and physical for risk stratification per AHA guidelines for acute chest pain.

MANDATORY: Immediate cath lab activation is required for primary PCI. Door-to-balloon target is <90 minutes. Patient has confirmed STEMI with dynamic ST changes — this is the most time-critical action.
MANDATORY: Aspirin 325mg chewable is first-line antiplatelet therapy for STEMI per AHA guidelines (Class I). No contraindications identified. Must be given immediately.

MANDATORY: Dual antiplatelet therapy with a P2Y12 inhibitor (ticagrelor or clopidogrel preferred given CKD stage 4 — avoid prasugrel if possible) is required per AHA STEMI guidelines. Reduces mortality and reinfarction risk.

MANDATORY action - Heparin or enoxaparin anticoagulation is required per STEMI/ACS guidelines as part of dual antiplatelet + anticoagulation therapy. This is the only remaining mandatory action and must be completed immediately.
Primary PCI must be arranged to meet door-to-balloon time target of <90 minutes. Cath lab has been activated; PCI arrangement is the next critical step to ensure timely reperfusion.

Serial high-sensitivity troponin measurement is Class I recommended per AHA guidelines for ACS diagnosis confirmation and risk stratification. Particularly important in this patient with CKD stage 4 where baseline troponin may be elevated.
IV access is essential for medication delivery in this NSTEMI/STEMI patient proceeding to PCI. This is a fundamental supportive measure needed before and during catheterization.

Critical safety step: must obtain right-sided ECG V4R to rule out RV infarction before administering nitrates. Per guideline, do NOT give nitrates if RV infarction is suspected (inferior STEMI pattern).

Cardiology consult is indicated for this high-risk NSTEMI/STEMI patient with CKD stage 4, diabetes, and hypertension proceeding to primary PCI. Specialist input needed for periprocedural management including contrast nephropathy risk given CKD stage 4.

ECG has been obtained but interpretation should be formally documented to guide ongoing management, confirm the infarct territory, and ensure no additional findings (e.g., right bundle branch block, reciprocal changes) are missed.

Patient is hemodynamically stable (HR 82, BP 155/88, SpO2 96%) without signs of heart failure or cardiogenic shock. Beta-blocker is indicated per AHA guidelines for NSTEMI/STEMI to reduce myocardial oxygen demand and risk of arrhythmia. CKD and diabetes are not contraindications here.

Patient has ongoing chest pain, hypertension (BP 155/88), and right-sided ECG has already been obtained to rule out RV infarction. If RV infarction is excluded, nitrates are indicated for symptom relief and BP management. Administer cautiously given CKD.
Comparing with prior ECG can help characterize the evolution of ST changes and confirm the working diagnosis of NSTEMI/STEMI, supporting appropriate management decisions.
Patient SpO2 is 96%, which is borderline. Supplemental oxygen should be considered to maintain SpO2 ≥94% per AHA guidelines for ACS management, especially given CKD and diabetes comorbidities.
If the patient continues to have chest pain at rest despite antiplatelet and anticoagulation therapy, analgesia with morphine may be considered for symptom relief while awaiting PCI.

At 90 minutes since arrival, door-to-balloon target is at the critical threshold. If PCI cannot be initiated immediately, fibrinolysis should be considered as a bridging strategy per STEMI guidelines, especially given the time-critical nature of reperfusion therapy.

Patient has CKD stage 4 and elevated BP (155/88). Cautious IV fluid support may be appropriate to maintain perfusion while awaiting PCI. Given CKD, conservative crystalloid fluid (not aggressive 30ml/kg bolus) is preferred to avoid fluid overload. This is an available optional action and no mandatory actions remain incomplete.

Patient has CKD stage 4 and hypertension with MAP of 110 mmHg. While all mandatory STEMI actions have been completed, cautious IV fluid support may be considered to maintain hemodynamic stability during PCI preparation. This is the only remaining available action not yet completed. Administer judiciously given CKD and hypertensive state.

Calculate GRACE or TIMI risk score to formally quantify risk and guide timing/intensity of invasive strategy. Patient has elevated troponin, dynamic ST changes, CKD stage 4, diabetes, and hypertension — high-risk features per AHA guidelines.

Patient has multiple high-risk features (elevated troponin 2.5x, dynamic ST changes, hypertension, diabetes, CKD stage 4). AHA Class I recommendation supports early invasive strategy within 24 hours for high-risk NSTEMI. Formal assessment needed to confirm eligibility and timing.

Patient with confirmed NSTEMI, elevated troponin, dynamic ST changes, and multiple comorbidities (CKD stage 4, diabetes, hypertension) requires continuous cardiac monitoring in CCU setting pending catheterization.
